title: Tesla profits drop 43% in Q3
gist: Tesla's Q3 2026 revenue of $28 billion was flat year over year while net profit fell 43 percent to $787 million, as operating expenses rose 39 percent, capex rose 110 percent and regulatory credit revenue collapsed to $113 million.

insights.claim: Tesla's Q3 2026 revenue was about $28 billion, almost unchanged from 2025, with automotive revenue down 3 percent to $20.6 billion.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Top-line stagnation with falling auto sales shows growth depends on non-auto lines.
insights.locator: Tesla published its third-quarter 2026 financial results

insights.claim: Solar and storage revenue fell 16 percent year over year to $2.9 billion, reversing a line that had been growing, while services and other revenue grew by a third to $4.6 billion.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Energy storage growth thesis took a hit this quarter; services is the offset.

insights.claim: Operating expenses rose 39 percent to $4.8 billion, cutting operating margin to 2.6 percent from 5.8 percent in Q3 2025, and net profit fell 43 percent to $787 million.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Margin compression from opex growth is the core earnings pressure.
insights.locator: But the company—like the rest of us

insights.claim: Capital expenditures rose 110 percent to $4.7 billion and free cash flow fell 62 percent to $1.5 billion.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Heavy AI hardware spend is draining free cash flow.

insights.claim: Regulatory credit revenue fell to $113 million from $417 million in Q3 2025 because other automakers now have EV portfolios and the US abolished such credits.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: A high-margin revenue source is disappearing structurally.
insights.locator: Tesla can no longer rely on selling regulatory credits

insights.claim: Tesla attributes flat revenue to lower average selling prices, fewer cars sold, lower credits and weaker energy storage; Ars adds that rising costs reflect AI hardware spending and the CEO's compensation package.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Both AI capex and governance cost items weigh on profitability.
